texts: good. the harvest lands as one past event with Coraline Ash as agent, salt-bloom as what was harvested, and the new moon and the date attached to it; a bare 'salt-bloom' object is read as the substance in general, which is the right reading here. One caveat not worth rewriting for: the translator has no term for a day-of-year or an era year, so 'day 33 of Year 1' is stored as a bare day number beside a year rather than as a well-formed date.

good. agent, the submerged stone group (with 'submerged' handed down to each stone), the pool those stones sit in, the wooden scraper as instrument and past tense are all covered. 'the second pool' is recorded as rank 2 in an improvised ordering — it reads true, so no rewrite is needed, though a question phrased around the pool's position may not resolve.

mixed: everything about the event is there (the stones as the source, and 'in pale flakes' with the flakes grouped and each one pale), but bare 'Salt-bloom' as the subject of a one-off past clause lands on the substance kind rather than on the specific batch being harvested, so what came off the stones is not the batch the rest of the passage tracks. Write "The salt-bloom came off the stones in pale flakes." — the definite gives it a specific referent that the later sentences can point back to.
good. the gathering reuses the flake group introduced by the previous sentence, with Coraline Ash as agent and the fine net as instrument.

mixed: the rotation, the harvest party, midnight and past tense are all recorded, but 'rotated pools' leaves it undecided whether 'pools' names a particular set of pools or just the activity of switching between them, and the parse minted a specific set — which the next sentence then reuses. Write "At midnight, the harvest party moved to different pools." (with the matching form in the next sentence) so each occasion gets a set of its own.

bad: this rotation is handed the very same pool group as the midnight one, so the parse asserts that both rotations involved the same pools — something your text never says. Write "At the third watch, the harvest party moved to different pools again." — 'again' is kept as the repetition marker, and a fresh set of pools is minted for this occasion.
good. one past inspection by the harvest party over a two-member group of southern pools, with the count, the 'pool' genus and the 'southern' property all unpacked.

mixed: the denial itself is recorded exactly right — the group did not bloom and neither did either pool, with 'that night' resolved back to day 33 of Year 1 — but the verb 'bloom' collapses onto the same symbol as the 'bloom' inside 'salt-bloom', so the substance kind and the blooming event stop being distinguishable. If you can spare the verb, write "The two southern pools did not yield salt-bloom that night."
good. 'the harvest' resolves back to the day-33 harvest and the dusk-to-dawn extent attaches to it as its start and end points, with no stray extra event invented for 'ran'.
